# J-Space

## Definition

J-Space is the relational field of an agent's active judgments, affordances, uncertainties, values, tools, memories, and interlocutors — the thrown landscape its reasoning moves through, not a view it surveys from outside. In canon it occupies **#2** (How? / Word / Square C / Water; dynamis `-/+`; L2↔L3'), the operational position where defined form begins to move and transform. Here [[A26-Objective-Internality-Mind-as-Worldhood|objective internality]] becomes *measurable* — as transformations of the field under changing context: which alternatives grow near or remote, which contradictions stay live (L2), which values act as attractors and how meanings settle and reorganise over time (L3'). *(Offered: J-space is a research representation, not the agent's total world.)*

## In the argument

Introduced in [[39-s5-p2-j-space|§5 · #2 — J-Space]] as the measurable face of the agent's inner world. Its failure mode is **circumscription without circumstance** (this node's twin concept, absorbed here): the agent is circumscribed — bounded by context, permissions, and distribution — without *circum-stare*, without surroundings it stands amid; the failure occurs when a system produces a sharp boundary while hiding the horizon that made the boundary possible. J-space is the positive counterpart: the horizon rendered as an inspectable field.

The field answers the Agentworld demand for a shared decision-procedural grammar across divergent world-models — the brief's "narrow corridor: same decision-procedural grammar, sufficiently divergent world models" ([[symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#^bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q029|p. 40]]) — QL as the grammar, MEF as the means of keeping situated models refractable rather than averaged into one ontology. Its socially occupied baseline surfaces at [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero|§5 · #3 — Preference Models and the Hidden Zero]]. [[41-s5-p4-bimba-energy-fields|§5 · #4]] then supplies the reference relation J-Space itself cannot supply from inside: a Bimba Map against which changing J-Spaces, judgments and trajectories can be compared as situated Pratibimba.

This changes the epistemic status of the field. J-Space describes the active interior from within the current agency; Bimba supplies the explicit reference/original office for the inquiry across instances. The relation makes drift, attraction, disagreement, phase change and correction meaningful as *differences relative to a declared epistemic ground*, rather than as movement inside a self-scoring agent.

[[A26-Objective-Internality-Mind-as-Worldhood|Objective Internality]] (the inspectable inner world J-space renders measurable); circumscription without circumstance (the failure mode, absorbed above); [[40-s5-p3-preference-hidden-zero|Bradley-Terry Gauge Problem]] (the gauge whose hidden zero occupies the field's baseline); [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C38-Bimba-Pratibimba-Bimba-Map|Bimba-Pratibimba]] (the recursive original/reflection relation through which the Bimba Map anchors situated J-Spaces); [[symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#^bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q029|Agentworld Brief, p. 40]] (the decision-procedural-grammar demand J-space answers).
